# Ai2 OLMo

Ai2 publishes data, code, recipes, W&B logs, and intermediate checkpoints for OLMo 2 and OLMo 3,
plus a model-ladder paper on predicting task performance from small runs. Two accounting papers
by Morrison et al. give the development vs. final-run split directly: roughly 50/50 for the OLMo 2
era (ICLR 2025) and 82/18 for the whole Olmo 3 pipeline (2026). Working notes with sources are in
`data/notes/olmo.md`.


## The number that matters: development vs. final-run compute

Morrison et al. (2026) account for the entire Olmo 3 pipeline (7B and 32B, Instruct and Think).
Of 8.34M H100-hours, development (experimentation, failed runs, ablations, synthetic data)
took 6.85M and the final runs 1.49M. That is an experiment-to-final ratio near 4.6 to 1, up from
about 1 to 1 in their OLMo 2-era paper.

```{python}
c = load.claims("ai2-olmo")
dev = float(c.loc[c["claim"].str.contains("development"), "value"].iloc[0])
fin = float(c.loc[c["claim"].str.contains("final"), "value"].iloc[0])
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8, 1.8))
plots.stated_split({"Final runs": fin, "Development": dev}, ax=ax, unit="H100-hours",
                   title="Olmo 3 pipeline: final runs vs development (Morrison et al. 2026)")
plt.show()
```

The rows below are the runs we can reconstruct individually. Losses are not yet transcribed
(they live in public W&B and comet.ml dashboards), so the loss-vs-compute curve is pending; the
run-size map shows the ladder and the released models on the parameters-vs-tokens plane.

## Narrative

**Process.** The OLMo 2 development pattern: architecture and stability changes ablated at 1B,
19 "microanneal" runs totalling 130B tokens to test individual data sources, then final stage-1
runs (1 to 1.2 epochs) and several stage-2 anneals weight-averaged into the released model.
Olmo 3 formalised this into per-source microanneals (5B target tokens plus 5B web) feeding
"integration tests" (full 100B midtraining anneals on candidate mixes).

**Ladder.** Bhagia et al. (2024) trained 16 ladder models (190M, 370M, 760M, 1.3B, each at 1x,
2x, 5x, 10x Chinchilla tokens) and predicted OLMo 2 7B-4T and 13B-5T task accuracy within about
2 points on four tasks and about 4 points averaged over eight. The ladder cost about 1% of the
targets' compute.

**Run management visible in the scripts.** The official training scripts show decisions the
papers do not: the Olmo 3 7B schedule was extended from 5T to 7T tokens mid-run and then
hard-stopped at one epoch (5.93T); the 32B midtraining branched at 5.50T while pretraining ran
on to 5.70T, so about 196B tokens of 32B pretraining were not used by the released model.

**Not yet reconstructable.** Per-task fitted coefficients from the ladder paper; the split of the
6.85M development hours across pretraining, midtraining, post-training and synthetic data; OLMo 2
7B and 13B GPU-hours; loss values (pending a pull from the public dashboards). arXiv was
unreachable from this environment, so paper numbers came via secondary summaries and Ai2's
GitHub repositories; the notes file lists 13 items to verify against the primary sources.
